boundary.internal: Host the insrc chat as an Activity Bar sidebar webview view

api.name: webviewViewToChannel

parameters.name: view
parameters.purpose: The sidebar view VS Code delivered to resolveWebviewView; its .webview is the render/message surface.

returns.meaning: A ChatPanelChannel (chat-panel.ts:29) backed by the resolved WebviewView: setHtml -> view.webview.html=; postMessage -> view.webview.postMessage; onMessage -> view.webview.onDidReceiveMessage; onDidDispose -> view.onDidDispose; reveal -> view.show(true); dispose -> no-op (VS Code owns the view's lifecycle). vscode-free at the type level.

errors.condition: Pure mapping; a postMessage to a hidden/disposed view is fire-and-forget (rejection swallowed, mirroring the panel channel).

preconditions: view.webview.options.enableScripts has been set true by the provider before the host renders the nonce'd shell.
postconditions: The returned channel drives createChatPanelHost exactly as the editor-panel channel does today.

api.name: createChatPanelHost

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: REUSED UNCHANGED. For the sidebar, deps.createPanel is supplied as () => webviewViewToChannel(resolvedView); providers/store/cwd/editGovernance are the same objects wired today.

returns.meaning: The existing chat host (chat-panel.ts:87); open() calls deps.createPanel() for the channel, wires onMessage/onDidDispose, setHtml(renderShell()), posts theme/session-restored/history, runs the unchanged turn-loop. NOT modified.

errors.condition: Behavior unchanged; the host is contract-stable (S003-owned).

preconditions: Constructed inside resolveWebviewView with a createPanel that returns the resolved-view channel.
postconditions: The chat renders in the sidebar view and behaves identically to the editor-tab chat.

api.name: createChatSidebarViewProvider

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Injected seams: { toChannel: (view) => ChatPanelChannel; makeHost: (createPanel) => ChatPanelHost; enableScripts: (view) => void; logger? }. Keeps the provider vscode-free/testable.

returns.meaning: resolveWebviewView(view) enables scripts, wraps the view via toChannel, builds the host with createPanel:()=>thatChannel, and opens it. Re-resolution rebuilds channel+host so a stale host never posts into a disposed view.

errors.condition: A postMessage after the view is disposed is swallowed; re-resolution supersedes the prior host (generation/current-view guard).

preconditions: Registered via window.registerWebviewViewProvider('insrc.chatView', provider) ONLY inside the if (chatEnabled) gate.
postconditions: Clicking the insrc Activity Bar icon shows the sidebar view rendering the chat.

api.name: insrc.chat.open
api.signature: commands.register({ id: 'insrc.chat.open', title: 'insrc: Open chat' }, () => vscode.commands.executeCommand('insrc.chatView.focus')): void

returns.meaning: EXISTING command (extension.ts:535), REPOINTED from opening an editor-tab panel to focusing the sidebar view via the auto-generated '<viewId>.focus' command. Same command id (no new InsrcCommandId).

errors.condition: executeCommand('insrc.chatView.focus') is a built-in command generated for the contributed view; reveals/focuses it.

preconditions: insrc.chat.enabled is true (command + view exist only under the gate).
postconditions: The insrc sidebar view is revealed and focused.

errorCases.scenario: The sidebar view id in package.json (insrc.chatView) does not match the id passed to registerWebviewViewProvider.
errorCases.detection: At runtime VS Code shows the view body empty / 'no view registered'; caught in dev by the manifest-vs-source assertion that both use the identical literal 'insrc.chatView'.
errorCases.response: Single-source the view id as one constant referenced by both the manifest-shape test and the provider registration; the wiring test asserts registerWebviewViewProvider is called with the exact contributed id.
errorCases.userImpact: Empty sidebar view (no chat) until the ids match.

errorCases.scenario: resolveWebviewView renders the nonce'd chat shell but scripts are disabled on the view's webview.
errorCases.detection: The webview loads but the inline bootstrap never runs (acquireVsCodeApi undefined); detectable because setHtml content shows but no session-restored render appears.
errorCases.response: The provider MUST set view.webview.options = { enableScripts: true } BEFORE the host renders; a wiring assertion checks enableScripts is set in resolveWebviewView.
errorCases.userImpact: A visible but inert chat (no streaming, no input) until scripts are enabled.

errorCases.scenario: VS Code disposes a hidden sidebar view and later re-resolves it while a stale host holds the old channel.
errorCases.detection: A post to the disposed webview rejects; the re-resolution path receives a fresh WebviewView instance distinct from the one the stale host captured.
errorCases.response: createChatSidebarViewProvider treats each resolveWebviewView as authoritative: it builds a fresh channel + host for the new view and lets the old host's channel dispose become a no-op / swallow late posts. postMessage stays fire-and-forget.
errorCases.userImpact: None when handled — the chat re-renders in the re-shown view; without the guard a stale turn could error silently.

errorCases.scenario: media/insrc.svg is missing from the packaged .vsix or the icon path is wrong.
errorCases.detection: Package-time the file is absent (.vscodeignore or wrong relative path); runtime VS Code draws a placeholder.
errorCases.response: Keep the SVG under media/, reference the correct relative path, add a packaging test asserting the file exists and the manifest icon path resolves.
errorCases.userImpact: Cosmetic — the container still works; a placeholder glyph shows instead of the insrc mark.

edgeCases.expected: The view's when-clause is false; VS Code hides the view and the whole insrc container/icon; the provider is not registered and insrc.chat.open is absent. No surface leaks.

edgeCases.input: insrc.chat.open is invoked from the command palette.
edgeCases.expected: It runs executeCommand('insrc.chatView.focus'), revealing + focusing the sidebar view (resolving + rendering the chat if not already shown).

edgeCases.input: The user collapses/hides the sidebar view, then reopens it.
edgeCases.expected: With retainContextWhenHidden:true the webview state is preserved where VS Code allows; otherwise re-resolution rebuilds the host and restores the active session from the ChatSessionStore. No duplicate sessions.
Chat still renders; cwd falls back to process.cwd() exactly as the editor-panel path does today.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The chat turn-loop, session store, provider registry, markers, and edit-governance are reused verbatim through createChatPanelHost via the ChatPanelChannel seam — this story does NOT modify createChatPanelHost or the ChatPanelChannel interface (chat-panel.ts:29/87).
The chat is driven ONLY through the ChatPanelChannel interface; the WebviewView is adapted to that exact interface, so host behavior is identical to the editor-panel channel.
No new command id is introduced; insrc.chat.open is reused (repointed to <viewId>.focus), so the InsrcCommandId union and the exact-set command tests (count 13) are unchanged.
The whole surface stays behind insrc.chat.enabled (default false): when disabled there is no Activity Bar container, no view, no provider, and no command.

extension.ts remains the sole vscode importer; the new adapter/provider factory (chat-view-channel.ts) is vscode-free (type-only vscode imports), mirroring the createChatPanelHost deps-injected idiom.

alternativesConsidered.name: WebviewView→ChatPanelChannel adapter, host reused unchanged (createPanel returns the resolved view)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A WebviewViewProvider resolves the sidebar view, wraps it as a ChatPanelChannel, and drives the EXISTING createChatPanelHost by injecting a createPanel that hands back that already-resolved view's channel.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add viewsContainers.activitybar (insrc -> media/insrc.svg) + views.insrc = [{ id:'insrc.chatView', type:'webview', when:'config.insrc.chat.enabled' }]. New vscode-free chat-view-channel.ts exposes webviewViewToChannel(view): ChatPanelChannel. extension.ts registers a WebviewViewProvider (inside the gate) whose resolveWebviewView enables scripts, wraps the view, constructs createChatPanelHost({ createPanel: () => channel, ...same deps }), and calls host.open(). insrc.chat.open -> executeCommand('insrc.chatView.focus'). createChatPanelHost NOT modified.
pros: Zero change to the S003-owned createChatPanelHost / ChatPanelChannel contract — turn-loop/session/markers/edit-governance run identically.
Pure adapter + provider in extension.ts (the sole vscode importer); adapter is vscode-free and unit-testable.
Copilot/Claude/Codex parity: one click renders the chat in the sidebar.
No new command id — exact-set command tests stay at 13.
cons: Slightly indirect: open() calls deps.createPanel() which ignores its arg and returns the pre-resolved view channel — a mild abuse of the createPanel seam.
Re-resolution must rebuild the channel + host; the provider needs a small guard so a stale host does not post into a disposed view.

alternativesConsidered.name: Explicit externally-provided channel entry on the chat host (host bind refactor)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a small createChatPanelHost option/entry that accepts an already-built ChatPanelChannel instead of creating one, and the provider passes the resolved-view channel to it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same manifest + adapter as a1, but refactor createChatPanelHost to accept an optional injected channel (deps.channel? or host.attach(channel)) that open() uses directly, falling back to createPanel otherwise. Provider builds the channel and calls attach/open.
pros: Cleaner semantics: the host explicitly supports 'a surface is provided to me'.
Same adapter/provider structure; unit-testable with a FakeChannel.
cons: Touches the S003-owned createChatPanelHost signature/contract + its tests — wider blast radius than a1 for a single new caller.
More change than the a1 adapter for no user-visible benefit.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: winnerRank 2: functionally equal and semantically cleaner, but 'partial' on nf-minimal-blast-radius because it modifies the S003 chat-host contract for one caller; a1 achieves the same reuse without touching that contract.

alternativesConsidered.name: Dedicated sidebar chat host module (separate from createChatPanelHost)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Write a new createChatSidebarHost that renders the shell and runs the turn-loop for a WebviewView directly, independent of createChatPanelHost.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new module owns the sidebar view lifecycle end to end (resolveWebviewView -> render shell -> run the turn-loop -> post events), reusing lower-level pieces but NOT createChatPanelHost. insrc.chat.open focuses the view.
pros: Full control over sidebar-specific lifecycle (visibility, retainContextWhenHidden).
cons: DUPLICATES the entire chat turn-loop/session/single-in-flight/cancellation that createChatPanelHost already implements and that cold reviews hardened (S003/S005) — two copies drift.
Largest surface + highest regression risk; contradicts the reuse the story requires.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: winnerRank 3: 'violates' both uv-reuse-turn-loop and nf-minimal-blast-radius by duplicating the entire chat turn-loop; highest regression risk.
